reason: The text portrays Israel as 'am' (עַם - people/nation) multiple times, explicitly distinguishing them from other named nations and peoples (Philistines, Edomites, Moabites, Canaanites). The Song emphasizes their collective national identity and destiny: they are described as 'the people whom you redeemed' (עַם־זוּ גָּאָלְתָּ) and 'the people whom you have acquired' (עַם־זוּ קָנִֽיתָ), being established as a distinct territorial entity ('your mountain of inheritance'). Other nations fear them as a people, not as individual devotees. While their identity is inseparable from their covenant relationship with Yahweh, the text portrays them as a structured national collective rather than merely a family or body of followers.
